title: Jonah 2 — The great fish and Jonah's prayer from its belly

verdicts.reasoning: wayman YHWH dāḡ gāḏôl ... bimʿê haddāḡ šəlōšâ yāmîm ûšəlōšâ lêlôṯ: 'prepared' (ASV) with 'appoint' in commentary, and 'a great fish' with no species. MT numbering is kept and the English equivalents are stated. The reception note quotes TBWTT ch. 3 ('Jonah, II-1') accurately and is labelled; the line does not identify the fish.

wayyiṯpallēl yônâ ʾel-YHWH ʾĕlōhāyw mimməʿê haddāḡâ: exact ('his God', F1). Non-blocking fix: the note (and the dag-gadol overlay rationale) attribute the two-fish midrash to Pirqe de-Rabbi Eliezer 10. That chapter tells of the fish's eyes and Leviathan, and the reviewer could not find a male/female fish there. The female-fish story is the one Rashi gives ad loc. from Midrash Yonah; verify and correct.
qārāʾṯî miṣṣārâ lî ... mibbeṭen šəʾôl šiwwaʿtî šāmaʿtā qôlî: exact; the third-to-second person shift is kept. 'She'ol' follows the central wohChoice.
wattašlîḵēnî məṣûlâ bilḇaḇ yammîm wənāhār yəsōḇəḇēnî ...: 'the depth' / 'the flood' with the nāhār ≠ mabbûl note; exact (Ps 42:8 verbatim).
nigraštî minneḡeḏ ʿênêḵā ʾaḵ ʾôsîp̄ ləhabbîṭ ...: MT ʾaḵ 'yet' kept, Theodotion/NRSV ʾêḵ reported. Exact.
ʾăp̄āp̄ûnî mayim ʿaḏ-nep̄eš təhôm yəsōḇəḇēnî sûp̄ ḥāḇûš ləroʾšî: 'soul' (ASV) with 'throat/neck' in commentary is acceptable under the stated consistency with v8.
ləqiṣḇê hārîm yāraḏtî hāʾāreṣ bəriḥêhā ḇaʿăḏî ləʿôlām ...: 'the earth with its bars' (ASV 'earth') keeps the underworld sense; the ASV supplement 'closed upon me' is rightly dropped. Exact.
bəhiṯʿaṭṭēp̄ ʿālay napšî ʾeṯ-YHWH zāḵārtî ...: exact.
məšammərîm haḇlê-šāwʾ ḥasdām yaʿăzōḇû: 'lying vanities' (ASV) and 'their own kindness' (central chesed) are exact, and both readings of ḥasdām are in commentary.
waʾănî bəqôl tôḏâ ʾezbəḥâ-llāḵ ... yəšûʿāṯâ laYHWH: exact; the psalm's quotation closes here.
wayyōʾmer YHWH laddāḡ wayyāqēʾ ʾeṯ-yônâ ʾel-hayyabbāšâ: exact. The reception note matches TBWTT ch. 3 ('Jonah, II-11') and is labelled; the line gives the fish no identity.

glossaryReview.reasoning: Approve the rendering: 'a great fish', 'prepared' and 'vomited out' are literal, and the canon's submarine reading is kept to labelled notes. Non-blocking factual fix, the same one as in the 2:2 note: the two-fish midrash is attributed to Pirqe de-Rabbi Eliezer 10, but the reviewer finds it in Rashi ad loc. (Midrash Yonah) and not in PRE 10. Verify and correct in both places.
Approve: MT numbering is checked against the source (11 verses, 2:1 = English 1:17), it is consistent with the corpus refId practice, and it matches the canon's 'Jonas, II-1 / II-11' citations.

direct is right for a presentation convention with no interpretive content. Verified in the lines: English names, 'the Lord YHWH' / 'the Lord', unquoted messenger formula (Jer 10:2, 18), quoted speech inside oracles and visions, and nəʾum 'declares' kept distinct from ʾāmar 'says' (Zech 4:6 against 5:4). Two open points are recorded under founder recommendations: F3, where the reviewer supports 'declares', and F4, where the reviewer supports ratification. Text identical in all five overlays (hash-checked).

citations: EZK-WOH-43:2 (divergent practice, checked in the data)
glossaryReview.reasoning: Philologically the line is sound: in every LP1 site ʾĕlōhîm is either YHWH or the foreign gods set against him, and 'God'/'gods' is the ASV/NRSV/NJPS rendering and the isaiah-woh practice. Flagged only because this is the open founder decision F1 (published ezekiel-woh prints 'Elohim'), a project-stance call on the corpus's most visible term. Reviewer recommendation: ratify 'God' for the Latter Prophets.
Approve. məṣûlâ and təhôm are kept distinct, the MT ʾaḵ is kept, and nep̄eš 'soul' with the concrete sense in commentary is defensible. The underworld ʾereṣ at 2:7 is well grounded.

reviewerReport.lensLeakageCheck: Checked all 11 lines in the English alone. No English line reads as interpretation. The canon-cited verses (2:1, 2:11) render the Hebrew at standard values, and each reception note is under its own 'Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim)' heading. Each note's quotation was verified against the canon text (TBWTT ch. 3 and ch. 5, FR/EN). Capitalisation (e.g. 'the Fish Gate') and vocabulary updates ('scroll', 'lampstand') are register or name conventions with lexical basis, not lens.
reviewerReport.escalationReportAdjustments: Initial verdicts on all 109 LP1 lines, 31 overlay entries and 27 central ops were formed from the chapters, the sources, the drafts, the overlays and the diff, and recorded before wave-lp1-editor-report.md was opened. After reading it, no verdict changed. The report's watch points were each re-tested: Zeph 1:18 'earth', Zeph 1:10-11 names, Zech 4:14, Zech 9:9, Jer 10:5 and the unquoted Jer 10:2-5. The report does not mention the two Zech 4 speech-line issues (4:10 quote boundary; 4:13 'answered'), which stand as revise. The founder points F1-F5 are answered below.

founderDecisionRecommendations.F1-isaiah-aligned-conventions: Ratify for the Latter Prophets: 'God', 'earth'/'land' by scope, lowercase 'spirit', 'create' and 'oracle' are each the ASV/NRSV/NJPS-backed rendering and keep the five books one volume with Isaiah. Harmonize Ezekiel at its next wave, not by retro-editing signed-off chapters. The 'God'/'Elohim' split is the one item the reviewer flags for explicit founder ratification, because it is a project-stance choice.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F2-officials-shofar-vs-isaiah: Align Isaiah to 'officials' (Isa 32:1; 40:23; 43:28) and 'shofar' (Isa 27:13) at its next pass; both are lexically better grounded and already corpus rulings. Then promote megillah/menorah/sarim/shofar to central entries as the report proposes. Keep the Exodus 25 'lampstand' dependency on the Exodus checklist.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F3-neum-declares: Adopt 'declares YHWH' corpus-wide. Zechariah has ʾāmar YHWH (4:6) and nəʾum YHWH (5:4) within a few verses, and Isaiah's 'says' for both (e.g. ISA-14:22, checked) erases a distinction the Hebrew makes. Align Isaiah later.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F4-unquoted-messenger-formula: Ratify. At Jer 10:2-6 the Hebrew does not mark where the oracle ends, and leaving it unquoted avoids inventing a boundary. Related: at Zech 4:9-10 the wave's own marks run YHWH's word into the messenger's answer, which is the reviewer's revise at ZEC-WOH-4:10.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F5-sons-of-fresh-oil: Ship 'the two sons of fresh oil'. It is the most literal rendering, lexically grounded (yiṣhār, no māšaḥ), and inferred is the honest label; 'anointed ones' stays in commentary for reception continuity. If the founder wants a gentler line, 'the two sons of oil' (ASV margin) is the conservative literal fallback.

paragraphs.text: וַיְמַ֤ן יְהוָה֙ דָּ֣ג גָּד֔וֹל לִבְלֹ֖עַ אֶת־יוֹנָ֑ה וַיְהִ֤י יוֹנָה֙ בִּמְעֵ֣י הַדָּ֔ג שְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה יָמִ֖ים וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה לֵילֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: And YHWH prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah; and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.

notes.official:
*wayman YHWH dāḡ gāḏôl* 'And YHWH prepared a great fish' (overlay `dag-gadol-great-fish-jonah-2`). *wayman*, the Piel of *mānâ* 'appoint, assign', is the verb the book uses for each of YHWH's appointed agents (the plant, the worm and the east wind, 4:6-8); 'prepared' is the ASV's word and is kept, while NRSV and NJPS have 'provided' (Sasson, *Jonah*, AB 24B, 1990). *dāḡ gāḏôl* is 'a great fish', with no species: the Old Greek *kētos* 'sea-monster', taken up in Matt 12:40, lies behind the English 'whale'. The verse is 1:17 in English Bibles. This translation keeps the Hebrew numbering, in which it opens chapter 2, so JNA-WOH-2:2-11 correspond to English 2:1-10 (overlay `mt-versification-jonah-2`). The hosted reference files for this chapter are the World English Bible in English numbering; the printed ASV (1901) was the comparison text.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 3) quotes this verse in the Hebrew numbering ('Jonas, II-1': 'Yahweh prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah. And Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights') and reads the 'great fish' as a submarine in which the creators could converse with Jonah and follow the political events of the time. The line translates *dāḡ gāḏôl* literally and does not identify the fish.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֣ל יוֹנָ֔ה אֶל־יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהָ֑יו מִמְּעֵ֖י הַדָּגָֽה׃

i18n.en: Then Jonah prayed to YHWH his God from the belly of the fish,

notes.official: *wayyiṯpallēl yônâ ʾel-YHWH ʾĕlōhāyw* 'Then Jonah prayed to YHWH his God' (`elohim-god-latter-prophets`; the draft's 'his Elohim' followed the Genesis-scoped central entry). *mimməʿê haddāḡâ* 'from the belly of the fish' has the feminine *dāḡâ*, against the masculine *dāḡ* of vv1 and 11. It is probably a collective or stylistic variant (GKC §122t), though a midrash makes it a second, female fish into which Jonah was transferred (Midrash Yonah, cited by Rashi ad loc.). The line renders both 'fish' (overlay `dag-gadol-great-fish-jonah-2`).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר קָ֠רָאתִי מִצָּ֥רָה לִ֛י אֶל־יְהוָ֖ה וַֽיַּעֲנֵ֑נִי מִבֶּ֧טֶן שְׁא֛וֹל שִׁוַּ֖עְתִּי שָׁמַ֥עְתָּ קוֹלִֽי׃

i18n.en: and he said: "I called out of my distress to YHWH, and he answered me; out of the belly of She'ol I cried, and you heard my voice.

notes.official: The psalm opens here and runs to the end of v10; the words quoted inside it at v5 take single quotes (`house-conventions-latter-prophets`). *qārāʾṯî miṣṣārâ lî* 'I called out of my distress' (central `tzarah-distress-tribulation-vocabulary`; cf. Ps 120:1; 18:7). *mibbeṭen šəʾôl* 'out of the belly of She'ol' (central `sheol-underworld-realm-of-the-dead`): the 'belly' (*mēʿeh*) of the fish in v2 becomes, in the psalm, the 'belly' (*beṭen*) of the underworld.

paragraphs.text: וַתַּשְׁלִיכֵ֤נִי מְצוּלָה֙ בִּלְבַ֣ב יַמִּ֔ים וְנָהָ֖ר יְסֹבְבֵ֑נִי כָּל־מִשְׁבָּרֶ֥יךָ וְגַלֶּ֖יךָ עָלַ֥י עָבָֽרוּ׃

i18n.en: For you cast me into the depth, in the heart of the seas, and the flood was round about me; all your breakers and your waves passed over me.

notes.official: *məṣûlâ* 'the depth' is kept distinct from *təhôm* 'the deep' of v6 (central `tehom`). *wənāhār yəsōḇəḇēnî* 'and the flood was round about me': *nāhār*, normally 'river', is the current of the cosmic sea (Ps 24:2; 93:3), not the Flood (*mabbûl*) of Gen 6-9 (overlay `lexical-cruxes-jonah-2`). *kol-mišbārêḵā wəḡallêḵā ʿālay ʿāḇārû* 'all your breakers and your waves passed over me' is verbatim Ps 42:8.

paragraphs.text: וַאֲנִ֣י אָמַ֔רְתִּי נִגְרַ֖שְׁתִּי מִנֶּ֣גֶד עֵינֶ֑יךָ אַ֚ךְ אוֹסִ֣יף לְהַבִּ֔יט אֶל־הֵיכַ֖ל קָדְשֶֽׁךָ׃

i18n.en: And I said, 'I am cast out from before your eyes; yet I will look again toward your holy temple.'

notes.official: *nigraštî minneḡeḏ ʿênêḵā* 'I am cast out from before your eyes' (cf. Ps 31:23). *ʾaḵ ʾôsîp̄ ləhabbîṭ* 'yet I will look again' is the MT (ASV); Theodotion and NRSV read *ʾêḵ* 'how shall I look again?', which turns hope into despair. The MT is kept (`mt-qere-textual-policy-latter-prophets`; overlay `lexical-cruxes-jonah-2`). *hêḵal qodšeḵā* 'your holy temple' is the sanctuary as a whole, the context clause of central `ulam-hekhal-devir-temple-three-room-plan-cross-corpus`.

paragraphs.text: אֲפָפ֤וּנִי מַ֙יִם֙ עַד־נֶ֔פֶשׁ תְּה֖וֹם יְסֹבְבֵ֑נִי ס֖וּף חָב֥וּשׁ לְרֹאשִֽׁי׃

i18n.en: The waters closed in around me, even to the soul; the deep was round about me; weeds were wrapped about my head.

notes.official: *ʾăp̄āp̄ûnî mayim ʿaḏ-nep̄eš* 'The waters closed in around me, even to the soul' (central `mayim`): in this idiom *nep̄eš* has its concrete sense 'throat, neck' (Ps 69:2; NRSV 'up to my neck'). The ASV's 'soul' is kept, with the concrete sense stated here (overlay `lexical-cruxes-jonah-2`). *təhôm* 'the deep' (central `tehom`). *sûp̄* 'weeds', the reeds or seaweed of *yam sûp̄*, the 'Sea of Reeds'.

paragraphs.text: לְקִצְבֵ֤י הָרִים֙ יָרַ֔דְתִּי הָאָ֛רֶץ בְּרִחֶ֥יהָ בַעֲדִ֖י לְעוֹלָ֑ם וַתַּ֧עַל מִשַּׁ֛חַת חַיַּ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָֽי׃

i18n.en: I went down to the bottoms of the mountains; the earth with its bars was about me forever; yet you brought up my life from the pit, YHWH my God.

notes.official: *ləqiṣḇê hārîm yāraḏtî* 'I went down to the bottoms of the mountains', their roots in the cosmic sea. *hāʾāreṣ bəriḥêhā ḇaʿăḏî ləʿôlām* 'the earth with its bars was about me forever': *hāʾāreṣ* is here the underworld, whose gates are barred against the dead (Exod 15:12; Ps 71:20; Sasson, AB 24B). The line has 'the earth', which keeps that sense, where the draft's 'the land' would mislead (`eretz-earth-or-land-latter-prophets`; overlay `lexical-cruxes-jonah-2`). The ASV supplies 'closed upon me'; the Hebrew has only *baʿăḏî* 'about / behind me'. *šaḥaṯ* 'the pit'. *YHWH ʾĕlōhāy* 'YHWH my God' (`elohim-god-latter-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: בְּהִתְעַטֵּ֤ף עָלַי֙ נַפְשִׁ֔י אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה זָכָ֑רְתִּי וַתָּב֤וֹא אֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ תְּפִלָּתִ֔י אֶל־הֵיכַ֖ל קָדְשֶֽׁךָ׃

i18n.en: When my soul fainted within me, I remembered YHWH; and my prayer came in to you, into your holy temple.

notes.official: *bəhiṯʿaṭṭēp̄ ʿālay napšî* 'When my soul fainted within me' (cf. Ps 142:4; 143:4; overlay `lexical-cruxes-jonah-2`). *ʾel-hêḵal qodšeḵā* 'into your holy temple', the phrase of v5 (central `ulam-hekhal-devir-temple-three-room-plan-cross-corpus`).

i18n.en: Those who regard lying vanities forsake their own kindness.

notes.official: *məšammərîm haḇlê-šāwʾ* 'Those who regard lying vanities': the plural *haḇlê* refers to idols, as in Ps 31:7 (`hevel-vanity-latter-prophets`; NRSV 'worthless idols'). *ḥasdām yaʿăzōḇû* 'forsake their own kindness' (central `chesed-solitary-covenant-kindness`; ASV 'their own mercy'): either the loyalty they owe, or the One who is their loyal love (Sasson) (overlay `lexical-cruxes-jonah-2`).

paragraphs.text: וַאֲנִ֗י בְּק֤וֹל תּוֹדָה֙ אֶזְבְּחָה־לָּ֔ךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָדַ֖רְתִּי אֲשַׁלֵּ֑מָה יְשׁוּעָ֖תָה לַיהוָֽה׃ (ס)

i18n.en: But I will sacrifice to you with the voice of thanksgiving; what I have vowed I will pay. Salvation belongs to YHWH."

notes.official: *bəqôl tôḏâ* 'with the voice of thanksgiving' (cf. Ps 42:5; 50:14). *yəšûʿāṯâ laYHWH* 'Salvation belongs to YHWH' (cf. Ps 3:9) closes the psalm and its quotation.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה לַדָּ֑ג וַיָּקֵ֥א אֶת־יוֹנָ֖ה אֶל־הַיַּבָּשָֽׁה׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And YHWH spoke to the fish, and it vomited out Jonah upon the dry land.

notes.official:
*wayyōʾmer YHWH laddāḡ* 'And YHWH spoke to the fish', and *wayyāqēʾ* 'it vomited out' Jonah 'upon the dry land' (*hayyabbāšâ*, the dry land of Gen 1:9-10 and of the sea crossing, Ex 14:16). The verse is English 2:10 (overlay `mt-versification-jonah-2`).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 3) quotes the verse ('Jonas, II-11': 'And Yahweh spake unto the fish, and it vomited out Jonah upon the dry land') and reads it as the submarine coming close to the shore and returning Jonah to dry land. The line translates *wayyāqēʾ* 'vomited out', as the ASV and NRSV do, and gives the fish no identity beyond the Hebrew (overlay `dag-gadol-great-fish-jonah-2`).
